newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends up on foreign stock limit news.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends up on foreign stock limit news.

text.p: The won closed higher against the dollar on Wednesday as dollar unwinding outweighed importer settlements, brokers said.
They said the dollar unwinding was caused by the news that the foreign shareholding limit would be raised on October 1.

"Dollar inflows are expected to rise when the limit is raised in October," said Park Se-gull of the Korea Exchange Bank. The finance ministry said on Tuesday the ceiling would be lifted to 20 percent from the current 18 percent.
The won closed at a high of 818.50 after opening at 818.80. It touched a low of 819.20.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 818.90 on Thursday, compared with 819.10 on Wednesday.
Dealers said the crisis in the Middle East stemming from the U.S. missle attacks on Iraq would strengthen the dollar in global markets.
But an expected rise in overseas corporate borrowings would offset some of the dollar's strength, they said.
"Factors for dollar supply and demand look balanced. We expect trading to be tightly ranged this month," said a Citibank dealer.
